priority_failure_modes.rationale: The plan must pre-specify one directionally interpretable primary endpoint, its patient-level aggregation, analysis population, time point and missing-data treatment; an endpoint selected or redefined after observing outcomes cannot support a falsifiable first-paper claim.

The inferential unit must be the patient, with repeated scribbles, joints and interaction steps treated as nested observations rather than independent samples; the target contrast, patient-level summary and patient-resampling uncertainty procedure must be explicit.

The no_M0 state must have a fixed neutralization rule that neither leaks M0-derived information nor gives one design a privileged placeholder, mask or fallback; the same rule must be used across all compared conditions.

Ambiguity strata must be defined from pre-outcome information with deterministic membership and minimum-support handling before analysis; post-hoc strata or outcome-informed thresholds would turn the mechanism test into exploratory selection.

Compared designs must share patient splits, input availability, training data, augmentation, optimization budget, backbone capacity, stopping rule and evaluation protocol, with any unavoidable asymmetry declared and isolated so the mechanism contrast is identifiable.

rejection_conditions: Reject if the primary endpoint, its direction, patient-level aggregation, analysis population, evaluation time point or missing-data rule is not frozen before outcomes are available.

Reject if the estimand treats scribbles, joints, lesions, slices or interaction steps as independent inferential units, or if uncertainty is not computed with patient as the resampling or clustering unit.
Reject if OOF M0 is not demonstrably patient-excluded, accesses target-patient labels or evaluation information, or is generated with any fold or oracle leakage.
Reject if the no_M0 neutralization is unspecified, differs across candidates or conditions, or can encode privileged M0-derived state.
Reject if ambiguity strata are outcome-defined, mutable after inspection, non-deterministic, or used to replace the frozen overall primary analysis without a pre-specified multiplicity policy.
Reject if comparator differences extend beyond the intended mechanism through unequal data, inputs, capacity, training budget, tuning access, stopping rules or evaluation procedures.
Reject if any candidate violates the fixed six-joint ontology or broadens the first-paper claim beyond the frozen operation, target and scope factors.
Reject if the design claims statistical evidence, empirical superiority, execution readiness or results despite the DESIGN_ONLY and runtime-unobserved boundary.

score_policy.winner_rule: Score each anonymous candidate independently on every frozen dimension Q1 through Q8 using the 0-4 scale. A candidate is winner-eligible only with zero fatal defects and scores of at least 3 on each of Q1, Q3, Q4 and Q6. Among eligible candidates, prefer the higher Q1-Q8 total; if totals tie, prefer the higher Q1+Q3+Q4+Q6 core subtotal; if that also ties, declare no unique winner. If neither candidate is eligible, declare no acceptable winner even when one has the higher score.
